leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members include B020 in their round-1 preferred configuration, the stated majority size, but only as part of different prizes and with different names. Aili, Aqvist and Linke propose a single-part prize for Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli on the same citation concept (PROTAC induced proximity with structure-guided degrader design). Chabes proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa and widens the citation to include the thalidomide-cereblon molecular-glue mechanism. Sparr would recognise only Crews and Deshaies for the PROTAC concept, as one of two parts alongside B049. Shared: the event-driven, catalytic mechanism is a new pharmacological principle and has been confirmed in many laboratories. Not shared: whether the third name is Ciulli or Handa, whether glues belong in the citation, and whether B020 stands alone or is paired.

Sparr alone proposes a two-part prize: Cullis for ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B049) and Crews and Deshaies for the PROTAC concept (B020). She argues the achievements are distinct (delivery chemistry and chemical biology) and that the 2023 Medicine prize recognised nucleoside modification, not the carrier. Aili, Chabes and Linke list B049 only as an alternative, and Sparr herself says attribution among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is unresolved.

Brzezinski alone prefers halide perovskite solar cells (Miyasaka, Park, Snaith) as a single-part prize for the decisive steps from first sensitised cell to durable solid-state cell to thin-film route. He acknowledges narrower opening support than B020 and contested credit (Gratzel, Seok, Kanatzidis). B005 appears as an alternative for Linke, Sparr and Zou.

Somfai alone proposes a two-part prize pairing a mature synthetic method, Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (Hartwig and Buchwald), with covalent targeting of mutant KRAS (Shokat). He treats the Buchwald-Hartwig attribution as the cleanest on the list and Shokat's concept as singular, while conceding that B059 may look like a second prize in an area covered in 2010. He lists B020 only as an alternative.

Zou alone prefers molecular-sieve catalyst design (Corma, Davis, Zones) and explicitly says it has the least opening support and that her field-closeness should be discounted. She names B020 and B005 as alternatives.

areas_of_agreement: Targeted protein degradation (B020) has the broadest support: it was ranked in the top three by six of eight members in the opening, and it appears in the round-1 preferred configuration of five members and as an alternative of two more (Somfai, Zou).
All members who discuss B020 describe event-driven, catalytic degradation through induced proximity as a new pharmacological principle and accept that the mechanism has been reproduced independently.
No member disputes that no PROTAC has been approved; the disagreement is only about how much weight that carries.
Every member who supports B020 identifies attribution as the main difficulty, specifically the exclusion of Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray or Ciulli under a three-name limit.
No member reports a candidate-specific conflict; all eight conflict notes state that none is apparent.
scientific_disputes: Whether B020 should be defined as heterobifunctional PROTAC design only (Aili, Aqvist, Linke, Sparr) or should also cover thalidomide-cereblon molecular glues (Chabes, with Brzezinski and Aqvist raising the issue).
Whether Handa's identification of cereblon is a design principle that generalises, or a target-identification result about an existing drug, as Aili argues against Brzezinski's and Chabes's position.
Whether ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B049) are chemistry, as Sparr argues from pKa-tuning, self-assembly and phase behaviour, or pharmaceutical technology, as she expects some members to say.

Whether next-generation sequencing (B014) is chemistry anchored in reversible-terminator nucleotide chemistry or mainly instrument engineering and platform scale-up, and whether Rothberg's pyrosequencing and semiconductor route belongs with the Solexa chemistry.
Whether Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B059) is a new principle or an extension of the reaction family recognised in 2010, and whether porous-material catalysts (B044) overlap with the 2025 MOF prize.
attribution_disputes: B020 third name: Aili, Aqvist and Linke choose Ciulli (structure-guided VHL design) while Chabes chooses Handa (cereblon); Aili would accept Handa if glues are to be covered but wants Ciulli's absence discussed. Sparr limits B020 to Crews and Deshaies. Ito, Sakamoto, Kim and Gray are excluded in every configuration.
B049: Sparr proposes Cullis alone and says this understates a team effort including Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer; she also notes that decisive optimisation occurred in companies.
B005: Brzezinski's trio omits Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis, and he asks whether the supplied list omits an early originator.
B014: members differ on whether the core is Balasubramanian and Klenerman alone or includes Rothberg, with Mayer and Ju as possible arbitrary exclusions.
B058 and B059: Shokat's credit versus the industrial developers (Amgen, Mirati), and Kosugi's and Migita's priority relative to Buchwald and Hartwig.
maturity_disputes: B020 has no approved PROTAC drug. Aili and Somfai treat this as a timing risk, Aqvist notes it could make the prize look rushed, Chabes says the work may be somewhat early, and Linke and Sparr treat it as a prospective payoff. Brzezinski notes that only the cereblon strand is attached to approved drugs.
B005 has unresolved long-term stability, lead toxicity and manufacturing questions (Brzezinski).
B058 has approved drugs but built by industry, with resistance and durability still limiting the clinical response (Somfai).
B014, B059 and B044 are described as mature by their proponents; the issue for them is novelty or overlap with earlier prizes (2002, 2010, 2020, 2025), not timing.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Zou flags field-closeness to B044 (electron crystallography of zeolites and other porous crystals) and asks colleagues to weigh her advocacy accordingly; she reports no tie to Corma, Davis or Zones.
Sparr notes that her research on lipid self-assembly and membranes is scientifically close to B049, with no personal or institutional tie to the candidates.

Chabes notes that his nucleotide-metabolism work is adjacent to the chemistry behind B014, with no recusal needed; Aqvist notes proximity to the computational fields of B053 and B050 through his postdoc connection with Warshel, with no collaborator among the credited names.
Aili notes adjacency to biosensors and nanoparticle work and that his postdoc mentor Molly Stevens is not credited on any shortlisted ballot.
Brzezinski and Zou are Stockholm University colleagues, and Linke, Somfai and Sparr share Lund University; all state this is not a candidate-specific link.
questions_for_round2: If B020 is the working base, should the citation cover PROTACs only (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) or PROTACs and cereblon glues (Crews, Deshaies, Handa), and can Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski and Chabes agree on a single third name?
Is the absence of an approved PROTAC drug a decisive timing objection for B020, and would members who raised it (Aili, Aqvist, Chabes, Somfai) still support B020 if it were the sole part?
Would Sparr maintain Cullis alone for B049 given Chabes's and Aili's doubts, and can any three-name or two-name B049 attribution be defended from the record?
Is a two-part prize (Sparr's B049 plus B020; Somfai's B059 plus B058) preferred to a single-topic prize, given that a three-person cap leaves each part with one or two names?
For B014, is the defensible core Balasubramanian and Klenerman, or does Rothberg belong, and can members who ranked it high (Chabes, Linke) say whether it is a chemistry prize?

What is the committee's view of the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the 2025 MOF prize as bars to B059 and B044, and can proponents of B005, B044 or B059 show that their candidate would outrank B020 on merit?
summary.chair_observation: B020 is the only candidate in more than one member's preferred configuration, with five supporters, but those five propose three different laureate sets and two different prize structures, so round 1 shows convergence on the topic and not on a prize. The other four configurations (B005, B059 with B058, B044) each have one explicit supporter, and two members who chose B020 as an alternative or second part also rank sequencing or nanoparticle delivery highly. I count only what the eight files state and do not infer further votes.
